metadata.title: Product Bricks & Streams
metadata.description: Hierarchical product brick map for the instant-photo-book-platform domain, modeled on PastBook (Amsterdam): the iOS and Android app and the pastbook.com web creator that import photos from the phone camera roll, Facebook, a computer, Dropbox or Google Drive, the intelligent curation engine that scores quality, removes duplicates and blurry shots, groups moments and lays out a book in under 60 seconds, the commerce stack of catalog, page rules, seven currencies, promotions, gift cards, checkout, payments and orders, the production chain of print-ready rendering, preflight, routing to partner printing facilities on four continents, shipping and SLA monitoring, the growth and 24/7 customer-care tooling, and the platform foundation of identity, photo media storage, privacy, analytics and the integration gateway to Meta, cloud drives, payment providers, carriers and app stores.

bricks.name: Mobile App Shell (iOS and Android)
bricks.description: The PastBook 1-Click Photo Book app for iOS and Google Play, with 1M+ downloads and App Store featuring in several countries (September 2022), is the primary consumer entry point since Instagram discontinued third-party access for personal accounts. The shell owns navigation, onboarding, photo-library permission prompts, remote configuration, feature flags, release management and the in-app review prompt, and hosts the import, curation, preview, editor and checkout surfaces as embedded flows. It also carries the wall-calendar products (small 8" × 11.7" USD 24.99, large 11.7" × 16" USD 34.99) that are only sold in the iOS app. Store compliance (privacy labels, App Tracking Transparency, Play Data Safety) is handled here so that every release passes review without blocking the Q4 campaign calendar.

bricks.name: Photo Library Access and Import (by date, location, album, Yearbook mode)
bricks.description: Imports photos from the phone camera roll, which is PastBook's primary source: the customer picks a date range, a location, an album or Yearbook mode (one year of photos), and the app indexes EXIF timestamps and locations, uploads the candidates over encrypted connections and hands the set to the curation engine. Uploads are chunked and resumable because a Family Memory Keeper may point the app at tens of thousands of photos on a mobile connection. The import session records which source, filter and permission scope produced the photo set so that curation, deletion and the 'my 2016' style yearbook reorder can be reproduced. Restoring source breadth after the Instagram loss makes this brick an investment area.

bricks.name: Instant Preview and Highlight Video Sharing
bricks.description: Shows the automatically designed book as a flippable preview for free within about a minute of choosing the photos, which is the moment PastBook wins or loses the order: the customer sees a finished book before paying anything. Since July 2023 the iOS app also renders a highlight video of the book that can be shared to the iOS share sheet, WhatsApp or social stories, bringing in friends and family as the cheapest acquisition channel. The preview keeps page thumbnails warm so that edits, theme changes and format switches (small 8.5" × 6" to large 12" × 8.5") re-render in seconds, and every preview carries the order call-to-action into the cart.

bricks.name: Web Book Creator
bricks.description: The pastbook.com creator that takes a customer from photo source to a free preview in about 60 seconds, orchestrating import, curation, layout and preview for the Facebook Photo Books and computer, Dropbox and Google Drive flows. It owns the book project, the central object that records source, selected photos, format, theme, edits and revision, and autosaves so a Traveller can return days later to finish a large hardcover. The creator serves ten site languages and shows prices in the customer's currency, and it is where the older, less technical Facebook Timeline Archivist spends most time, so it is kept deliberately linear with few decisions.

bricks.name: Upload from Computer, Dropbox and Google Drive
bricks.description: Lets web customers upload photos from a computer folder or connect Dropbox and Google Drive and pick folders or albums, the route PastBook promotes for people whose photos are not on the phone or Facebook. Cloud connections are OAuth-based with the narrowest scope the providers allow, tokens are stored encrypted and revoked after the book is produced or on request, and fetches run asynchronously so a 3,000-photo holiday folder does not block the browser. Files arrive over encrypted connections, are checked for supported formats and size, and are handed to media storage with their EXIF intact so the curation engine can group by time and place.

bricks.name: Facebook Connect and Year Selector
bricks.description: Powers the Facebook Photo Books product: after Facebook Login the customer sees one book per year from 2009 to 2025 assembled from albums, timeline pictures, cover and profile photos and mobile uploads, with captions and dates carried into the book. The crawl runs inside the permission scope Meta grants (user_photos) and under Meta Platform Terms, which require deleting data on request and not retaining it beyond the order, so tokens and downloaded photos have explicit expiry. It is the main flow of the Facebook Timeline Archivist and the fallback PastBook points Instagram users to since Instagram discontinued third-party access for personal accounts, which makes Graph API version deprecations and app review a permanent operational risk.

bricks.name: Page and Photo Editor (reorder, swap, remove, captions)
bricks.description: The optional editing step after the automatic design: reorder pages, swap or remove photos, pull back a photo the curation engine dropped, add captions and dates and fix crops. Every change is validated against the cover rules (up to 16 pages softcover, 18–26 pages a choice of soft or hard cover, 27–300 pages hardcover, above 300 softcover) and the price impact of extra pages (USD 0.40 small, USD 0.55 large) is shown live. Most Family Memory Keepers never open it, which is the strategic aim, while Travellers and Milestone Celebrants use it heavily for cover photo, order and captions; edit rate per segment is a core curation-quality signal.

rootGroups.name: Intelligent Curation Engine
rootGroups.description: PastBook's patent-pending curation technology, launched in the AI app in July 2021: it analyses image quality and context, removes duplicates and blurry shots, groups thousands of photos into moments, selects the best ones for the target page count and lays out a themed book in under 60 seconds, so the customer previews a finished book without designing anything.

subGroups.name: Photo Analysis
subGroups.description: Quality scoring, duplicate detection, moment grouping and best-photo selection over the imported photo set.

bricks.name: Image Quality Scoring (blur, exposure, resolution)
bricks.description: Scores every imported photo for technical quality: blur and motion, exposure and contrast, resolution against the print size (a 12" × 8.5" large hardcover spread needs far more pixels than a small book page), faces present and eyes open, screenshots and receipts. Scores are produced within seconds of ingestion so the 60-second book target holds even for a 5,000-photo yearbook import, and they are the first filter that removes the blurry shots PastBook promises to drop. Scores are stored per asset and reused across books, re-imports and reorders, and are purged with the photo when a customer deletes their data.
